headline: Resolution objecting to Pioneer Charter School of Science's expansion application passes unanimously
summary: The application is before the state Department of Elementary and Secondary Education. During public comment, speakers said the expansion would hurt schools in Salem and seven other communities. A policy banning smart glasses and wearable recording devices passed first reading. A consent agenda, including a Salem High basketball trip to Orlando, was also approved.
decisions: Approved the consent agenda: October 19 minutes, a Salem High basketball trip to Orlando, and two warrants, unanimously.
Approved first reading of a policy prohibiting smart glasses and wearable recording devices, unanimously.
Adopted a resolution objecting to Pioneer Charter School of Science's expansion application, unanimously.
discussion: School resource officers: Principals described officers' work at their schools, including relationship-building and emergency response. Members asked for a special meeting and for discipline data, and the updated memorandum of understanding is due by August 1st under state law.

Bus service and stop arms: The finance and operations report said the bus contract costs about $500 a day for 12 buses, and weekday athletic trips sometimes left late. A Bus Gate stop-arm trial is being set up on a district bus, with an update planned for the next meeting.

Smart glasses policy: The policy bans covert recording devices, including smart glasses and wearable AI voice recorders, with exceptions the superintendent or their designee may allow for educational needs. A separate policy on AI use in schools may be drafted with help from MASC.

Pioneer charter expansion: During public comment, speakers said the expansion would hurt schools in Salem and seven other communities. Speakers asked the board to vote on a resolution against it, which passed unanimously.
